steps.question: Does the engine turn over normally?
Do you have a strong spark at the plug?
Is fuel reaching the engine?
Does the engine have normal compression?
Did it fail suddenly, or did the kickstarter become unusually easy?

mechanical-lock.title: Mechanical problem suspected
mechanical-lock.text: Stop forcing the engine. Check for a seized engine, transmission lock-up, starter mechanism, or another mechanical obstruction.

ignition.title: Ignition system suspected
ignition.text: Inspect the plug, cap, coil, wiring, grounds, kill switch, stator/pickup, and ignition system.

fuel-system.title: Fuel delivery suspected
fuel-system.text: Check the fuel valve, line, filter, carburetor or injector, float system, and fuel delivery.

compression-fault.title: Compression problem suspected
compression-fault.text: Check valve clearance, valve sealing, cam timing, decompressor system, piston, rings, and head gasket.

timing-check.title: Timing should be checked first
timing-check.text: Stop repeated starting attempts and verify cam timing, timing-chain condition/tension, and crank timing before replacing parts.

general-check.title: Systematic diagnosis recommended
general-check.text: Verify spark, fuel, compression, air supply, and ignition timing systematically before replacing components.

steps.question: Is the spark plug clean, correctly gapped, and not damaged?
Is the plug body properly grounded against the engine while testing for spark?
Is the kill switch and ignition wiring working normally?
Does the ignition coil and plug cap pass the model's resistance/continuity checks?
Does the stator/pickup output meet the model-specific service specification?
Are connectors, grounds, and wiring clean and secure?

plug.title: Spark plug is the first suspect
plug.text: Replace or correctly gap the plug, then retest spark using the correct procedure for the bike.

ground-check.title: Correct the spark test
ground-check.text: Use a clean metal engine ground and follow the bike's specified spark-testing procedure.

kill-switch.title: Kill switch/wiring suspected
kill-switch.text: Inspect the kill-switch circuit, ignition switch, connectors, grounds, and damaged wires.

coil.title: Ignition coil or cap suspected
coil.text: Test the coil and plug cap against the service manual specifications before replacement.

stator.title: Stator/pickup suspected
stator.text: Test stator and pickup outputs using the model-specific service procedure and specifications.

wiring.title: Wiring or ground fault suspected
wiring.text: Repair loose, corroded, broken, or damaged wiring and grounds, then retest spark.

ignition-module.title: Ignition module is a later suspect
ignition-module.text: If plug, controls, coil, stator/pickup, wiring, and grounds test good, diagnose the ignition control module using the service manual.

steps.question: Is there fresh fuel in the tank and is the fuel valve turned on?
Does fuel flow normally from the tank through the fuel line?
Is the carburetor bowl filling, or is the injector receiving fuel pressure as specified?
Is the intake path clear and is the air filter serviceable?
Does the bike still fail after confirming fuel and air delivery?

fuel-supply.title: Fuel supply problem
fuel-supply.text: Add fresh fuel if needed and verify the fuel valve, tank vent, and fuel supply configuration.

line-filter.title: Fuel flow restriction
line-filter.text: Inspect the fuel line, filter, petcock, tank screen, and tank vent for blockage or restriction.

delivery.title: Carburetor/injector delivery problem
delivery.text: Check carburetor float/needle operation and passages, or verify injector pressure and operation on fuel-injected models.

intake-restriction.title: Intake restriction
intake-restriction.text: Clean or replace a blocked air filter and inspect the intake tract for obstructions or damage.

deeper.title: Fuel/air system needs deeper testing
deeper.text: Confirm fuel pressure or carburetor settings, injector operation, intake leaks, and model-specific mixture controls.

general-check.title: Fuel and air are likely present
general-check.text: Move to spark, compression, timing, and other system checks instead of replacing fuel-system parts blindly.

steps.question: Are valve clearances within the model-specific specification?
Does a compression test confirm low compression using the correct test procedure?
Does a leak-down test show significant leakage past the valves, rings, or head gasket?
Is cam timing correctly aligned with the crank at top dead center?

valve-adjust.title: Valve clearance problem
valve-adjust.text: Correct valve clearance to the exact model specification, then repeat the compression test.

test-procedure.title: Verify the compression test
test-procedure.text: Repeat the test with the correct gauge, throttle position, decompressor procedure, and model-specific method.

leak-source.title: Internal sealing problem suspected
leak-source.text: Use leak-down results to identify valve leakage, ring/cylinder leakage, or a head-gasket sealing problem.

cam-timing.title: Cam timing problem
cam-timing.text: Stop running the engine and verify cam timing, timing-chain condition/tension, and crank timing before further testing.

engine-wear.title: Engine wear is possible
engine-wear.text: Inspect piston, rings, cylinder condition, valve sealing, and decompressor operation according to the service manual.

steps.question: Is the coolant level correct and is there no obvious coolant leak?
Are the radiator fins clear and is coolant able to circulate?
Does the cooling fan operate when the bike reaches the specified temperature?
Is the fuel mixture/engine tune correct for the bike and conditions?
Does the water pump and thermostat system operate according to the service procedure?

coolant.title: Coolant level/leak problem
coolant.text: Let the engine cool completely, then inspect coolant level, hoses, radiator, water pump area, and leaks. Never open a hot cooling system.

radiator.title: Radiator airflow/circulation problem
radiator.text: Clean blocked fins carefully and diagnose restricted coolant circulation before riding again.

fan.title: Cooling fan problem
fan.text: Check the fan, fuse, relay, temperature switch/sensor, wiring, and power supply using the service procedure.

tune.title: Engine tuning problem
tune.text: Verify jetting or fuel-injection settings, intake leaks, exhaust condition, and model-specific tuning requirements.

cooling-system.title: Cooling-system component problem
cooling-system.text: Inspect the water pump, thermostat, hoses, radiator cap, and circulation system according to the service manual.

timing.title: Check timing and engine condition
timing.text: If the cooling system is operating correctly, verify ignition/cam timing and inspect for engine-condition problems that can create excess heat.

steps.question: Does it backfire mainly through the intake when opening the throttle?
Are there signs of a lean condition or an intake air leak?
Does it backfire mainly through the exhaust during deceleration?
Are ignition and cam timing confirmed to be correct?

intake-leak.title: Intake leak/lean condition suspected
intake-leak.text: Inspect intake boots, carburetor mounting, injector seals, vacuum lines, and fuel/air settings.

exhaust-leak.title: Exhaust leak suspected
exhaust-leak.text: Inspect exhaust joints, gaskets, and cracks for air entering the exhaust system.

timing-check.title: Timing problem suspected
timing-check.text: Verify ignition timing and cam timing against the model-specific service procedure before replacing parts.

fuel-ignition.title: Fuel or ignition system needs testing
fuel-ignition.text: Check mixture/fueling, spark quality, plug condition, and ignition timing systematically.

steps.question: Is the noise loud, metallic, rapidly worsening, or accompanied by loss of oil pressure/power?
Can you identify whether the noise is from the top end, bottom end, clutch, or transmission area?
Is the noise clearly from the top end/valve-cover area?
Does the noise change with engine RPM or when the clutch is operated?

stop-engine.title: Stop running the engine
stop-engine.text: Do not continue riding. Inspect oil level, engine condition, timing components, and other possible mechanical failures before restarting.

top-end.title: Top-end inspection recommended
top-end.text: Inspect valve clearance, camshaft, cam-chain/tensioner, decompressor, rocker/follower components, and lubrication.

bottom-end.title: Bottom-end inspection recommended
bottom-end.text: Inspect oil level/condition and diagnose crankshaft, rod, bearing, piston, and transmission components as appropriate.

isolate.title: Isolate the noise source
isolate.text: Compare the noise with engine RPM and clutch operation, then inspect the affected system using the service manual.

external.title: Inspect external components
external.text: Check skid plate, exhaust, chain, sprockets, mounts, guards, and other loose components that can create noise.
